Hi Elena —

Thanks for the clear list. I attached an updated term sheet that annotates our intended definitions; below are the short answers so your CFO/procurement can paste them into your checklist: 

1) Capacity unit definition (short):
   - "1 Capacity Unit (CU) = 1 GPU-Hour Equivalent (GHE) at 32GB FP16 baseline".
   - We normalize various hardware and model families into GHE using an internal benchmark (published in the model catalog) so billing is consistent across mixed-model workloads.

2) Throughput SLA mapping (short):
   - Throughput guarantees are provided at the committed CU level and expressed as a sustained token-generation rate for a reference workload (default: 2k tokens/sec per 8 CUs for the Llama-2-13B family, seq=1024).
   - For mixed models/seq lengths we map to an equivalent CU consumption using per-model token-cost multipliers (included in the annotated term sheet).

3) Service credits policy (short):
   - Credits accrue when p99 latency or sustained throughput falls below the committed target for >30 minutes.
   - Monthly cap = 50% of that month’s committed service fees (we can discuss lowering depending on tier).

I’m looping Ben for pricing/discount details and Priyom for the precise normalization language we should lock into the contract. If we can align on these three points, we’ll push a redline to you by EOW.

Cheers,

Avery/Marissa —

Draft language I think protects both sides and is implementable: 

"Capacity Unit (CU) means a GPU-Hour Equivalent (GHE) computed as the energy-normalized projection of a model’s sustained token-generation throughput on a 32GB FP16 baseline. Redwood will publish per-model multipliers in the model catalog that convert model-seconds and sequence-length into CU consumption. BlueCrest may request a one-time technical validation run for their primary models to confirm multipliers; any variance >10% will be reconciled by adjusting billed CUs for the first billing cycle post-launch."

Notes:
- This keeps the billing deterministic while allowing per-model nuance.
- We should add a clause for mixed-model bursts where billing falls back to actual measured GHE for that billing month.

Thoughts?
